test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 5 Oct 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A container in the shape of a right circular cone, whose radius and depth are equal, gets completely filled by 128000 spherical droplets, each of diameter 2 mm. What is the radius (in cm) of the container?
solution:
Given:

A container in the shape of a right circular cone, whose radius and depth are equal.

It gets completely filled by 128000 spherical droplets, each of diameter 2 mm.

Concept used:

Volume of a right circular cone = 1/3π × R² × H

when R, H are the radius and height respectively.

Volume of a sphere = 4/3 πr³

where R is the radius of the sphere.

Diameter = 2 × Radius

Calculation:

Let the radius and height be of right circular cone be R (mm).

According to the question,

1/3 × πR² × R = 128000 × 4/3 × π(2/2)³

⇒ R = 80

So, the radius of the container becomes 80 mm i.e. 8 cm

**∴ 8 cm is the radius of the container.**
